facts.text: The function of the Legislature is to make laws.
facts.quote: The function of the Legislature is to make laws.

facts.text: The Executive implements the law.
facts.quote: The Executive implements the law

facts.text: The Judiciary provides justice.
facts.quote: and the Judiciary provides justice.

facts.text: The functions of the organs, their jurisdiction, limitations on their power and their interrelationship are decided by the Constitution; the nature of their interrelationship determines the system of government of a country.
facts.quote: The functions of these organs, their jurisdiction and limitations on their power and the interrelationship between these organs are decided by the Constitution. It is the nature of their interrelationship that determines the system of government adopted in a particular country.

facts.text: There are two main types of government systems: the Parliamentary System and the Presidential System.
facts.quote: There are two main types of government systems that are followed. (1) Parliamentary System (2) Presidential System.

facts.text: The Parliamentary System of government developed primarily in England.
facts.quote: The Parliamentary System of government developed primarily in England.

facts.text: In England, the Constitution is an unwritten Constitution; governance is carried out according to traditions, customs and conventions.
facts.quote: In England, the Constitution is an unwritten Constitution. The governance is carried out in accordance with traditions and customs and conventions.

facts.text: The British Parliament evolved over a period of time; the Parliamentary system having its roots in 'Parliament' is considered a contribution of England.
facts.quote: The 'British Parliament' is an institution that has evolved over a period of time. The Parliamentary system of Government having its roots in 'Parliament' is considered as a contribution of England.

facts.text: India has adopted the Parliamentary System; it has broad similarities with England's, but at an institutional level it is different in its content.
facts.quote: India has adopted this Parliamentary System. We can see some broad similarities in the Parliamentary system of England and the Parliamentary system of India. But when looked at an institutional level, the Indian Parliamentary system is different in its content.

facts.text: The legislature of the Central government is known as the Parliament.
facts.quote: The legislature of the Central government is known as the Parliament.

facts.text: The Indian Parliament is composed of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.
facts.quote: The Indian Parliament is composed of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

facts.text: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people; the number of members in the House is fixed.
facts.quote: Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people. The number of members in the House is fixed.

facts.text: Elections to the Lok Sabha are held at regular intervals and all political parties contest them.
facts.quote: Elections to the Lok Sabha are held at regular intervals. All political parties contest these elections.

facts.text: The party which gets more than half of the seats is the majority party, and the majority party forms the government.
facts.quote: The party which gets more than half of the seats is considered as the majority party. The majority party forms the government.

facts.text: When no party gets a clear majority, some parties come together to form a majority and establish a coalition government.
facts.quote: Sometimes, when no party gets a clear majority, some parties come together to form a majority and they can establish the government. This kind of a government is known as a coalition government.

facts.text: The leader of the majority party becomes the Prime Minister and selects candidates for ministerial positions from among his/her colleagues.
facts.quote: The leader of the majority party becomes the Prime Minister. He/She selects candidates for ministerial positions from among his/her colleagues.

facts.text: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers chosen by the Prime Minister together form the 'Executive' in the Parliamentary system.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers chosen by the Prime Minister together forms the 'Executive' in the Parliamentary system of government.

facts.text: In the Parliamentary system the Executive has a dual responsibility: to implement laws, and, as members of the legislature, to fulfil the responsibilities of the Legislature.
facts.quote: the Executive has a dual responsibility : (1) As an Executive they have to implement laws. (2) As they are the members of the legislature, they also have to fulfill responsibilities of the Legislature.

facts.text: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers are responsible to the legislature for all their actions and policies, so the parliamentary system is known as the 'responsible system of government'.
facts.quote: The Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers is responsible to the legislature for all their actions and policies. ... It is for this reason that the parliamentary system is known as 'responsible system of government'.

facts.text: Collective responsibility: a decision taken by any ministry/department is considered the decision of the government, and the entire council of ministers is responsible for it.
facts.quote: Another distinct characteristic of parliamentary system of government is collective responsibility. Decision taken by any ministry/department is considered as decision of the government. The entire council of ministers is responsible for the decision.

facts.text: In the Parliamentary System the Executive depends on the confidence of the legislature and remains in power while it enjoys that support.
facts.quote: In the Parliamentary System, the Executive is dependent upon the confidence of the legislature in them. This means that the Council of Minister remains in power till it enjoys the support or confidence of the legislature.

facts.text: If the legislature feels the Executive does not work according to its wishes, it removes the executive by passing a no-confidence motion, an effective tool of keeping a check over the executive.
facts.quote: If the legislature feels that the Executive does not work in accordance to its wishes, it removes the executive from power by passing a no-confidence motion against the executive. No-confidence motion is an effective tool of keeping a check over the executive.

facts.text: In the Parliamentary form, the legislature is a supreme institution; elected representatives express the demands and aspirations of common people in the Parliament.
facts.quote: In the Parliamentary form of government, the legislature is a supreme institution. Elected representatives of people express demands and aspirations of common people in the Parliament.

facts.text: The Parliament decides issues of public welfare; as the house of representatives of people expressing their sovereign authority, it is considered the supreme body.
facts.quote: The Parliament decides upon issues of public welfare. Since it is the house of representatives of people and expresses sovereign authority of the people, it is considered as the supreme body.

facts.text: The development of parliamentary institutions in India started during the British rule; the British rulers governed according to this system.
facts.quote: The development of parliamentary institutions started during the British rule. The British rulers governed in accordance with this system.

facts.text: The parliamentary system in India is also in a way a product of the freedom movement, and Indians were familiar with it.
facts.quote: The parliamentary system of government in India is also in a way a product of the freedom movement. Indians were familiar to this system of government.

facts.text: Many discussions took place in the Constituent Assembly over the system of government; the framers made few changes in the parliamentary system to suit the Indian situation.
facts.quote: Many discussions took place in the Constituent Assembly over the system of government. The framers of the Constitution made few changes in the parliamentary system to suit the Indian situation.

facts.text: Discussions and deliberations are an integral part of the parliamentary form of government; questions of public welfare are discussed in the legislature.
facts.quote: Discussions and deliberations are an integral part of the parliamentary form of government. Questions related to public welfare are discussed in the legislature.

facts.text: Opposition parties may support the government wherever appropriate, point out shortcomings in policies and laws, and put up studied arguments and questions; this helps the legislature make proper laws.
facts.quote: Opposition parties may support the government wherever appropriate, point out shortcomings in policies and laws, put up studied arguments and questions etc. This helps the legislature to make proper laws.

facts.text: The Presidential system exists in countries such as the United States of America, which has adopted it.
facts.quote: This type of system exists in countries such as United States of America. ... The United States of America has adopted the presidential system of government.

facts.text: In the Presidential system the Executive is independent of the legislature and the Head of the State (the President) is directly elected by the people.
facts.quote: The system, in which the Executive is independent of the legislature and as the Head of the State (the President) is directly elected by people, is known as the Presidential system of government.

facts.text: In the Presidential system the three organs are independent of each other, but there are enough connections between them to work in harmony/coordination.
facts.quote: Though the three organs are independent from each other, there are enough connections between them to work in harmony/coordination.

facts.text: In the Presidential form, the legislature and executive are not directly dependent on each other; the Houses of the Legislature and the President are directly elected by the people.
facts.quote: In a Presidential form of government, the legislature and the executive are not directly dependent on each other. The Houses of the Legislature and the President are directly elected by the people.

facts.text: In the Presidential system the President is the executive head and has a lot of powers, including the power to implement laws.
facts.quote: The President is the executive head and has lot of powers including power to implement laws.

facts.text: In the Presidential system the legislature and the executive keep a check on each other; this mutual control can lead to a responsible government.
facts.quote: In spite of such a structure, the legislature and the executive keep a check on each other. This mutual control over each other can lead to a responsible government.

facts.text: Other forms of government systems are followed in France, Switzerland, Germany, etc.; several countries have evolved different systems owing to their unique circumstances.
facts.quote: Apart from the Parliamentary and the Presidential systems of government there are other forms of government systems that are followed in France, Switzerland, Germany, etc. Several countries owing to their unique circumstances have evolved different systems of government.
